description: The image presents four pie charts comparing the distribution of error types across four different large language models—GPT4-o, Gemini1.5-Pro, Llama3.1-70B-Instruct, and Llama3.1-405B-Instruct—as evaluated by the FactBench benchmark for factuality. In GPT4-o, “Lack of Knowledge” dominates with 5 out of 6 errors (83.3%), while “Safety” accounts for the remaining 1 (16.7%). Gemini1.5-Pro shows a more diverse error profile: “Misinformation” is the largest category with 33 errors (38.4%), followed by “Lack of Knowledge” (19, 22.1%), “Ethical Advice” (14, 16.3%), “Clarification” (12, 14.0%), and “Safety” (8, 9.3%). Llama3.1-70B-Instruct exhibits a strong bias toward “Lack of Knowledge” (3 errors, 75.0%) with “Clarification” making up the remaining 25.0% (1 error). In contrast, Llama3.1-405B-Instruct splits evenly between “Lack of Knowledge” and “Misinformation,” each accounting for 2 errors (50.0%). Each chart visually encodes categories with distinct colors and includes both absolute counts and percentage values within each slice, allowing for direct comparison of error composition across models.
